messages:
natalie: Heads-up — FP8 enablement smoke tests on H100/L40S after TE 2.3.2 rollout. Seeing two things: intermittent output divergence (rare) and a 20-40% tail latency regression for short-sequence requests when KV cache hit rates drop. Posting traces + quick notes.

natalie: nsys traces: `nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --trace=cuda,osrt python run_perf.py --model xrt-medium`
```
# summary (condensed)
Time   Kernel                       Avg (ms)
0.6ms  cutlass_attn                 0.6
1.9ms  fused_fp8_attn               1.9
SM eff: cutlass 94% | fused_fp8 68%
```

natalie: The selector is choosing fused_fp8_attn for many micro-batches when seq_len fluctuates (KV miss paths), despite cutlass being faster for the short sequences. suspect kernel_selector favors fp8 path due to accuracy heuristics and worst-case seq_len sampling.

dmitri: I saw similar on L40S in staging. When KV hit rate >90% the FP8 path shines. But when hit rate drops to ~50% the fused kernel ends up doing extra work (repacking + dequant) per-step. that overhead dominates.

ryan: Quick workaround: flip fp8 fallback to int8 for short-seq models. Config experiment I ran: `transformer_engine.fp8_fallback_seq_threshold=64` — if max_seq <=64 use INT8 kernels. latency down ~25% and no divergence.

ashley: Another lever is batching heuristics. Our current batcher uses max_seq to pick kernel. That punishes mixed-length workloads. Proposal: sample the last N requests and pick kernel based on 90th percentile seq_len, or use dominant bucket heuristic. small patch in batcher yields ~10% avg improvement in mixed workloads.

natalie: Good point. We should also measure KV cache churn. If many requests are cold-starting kv, the extra quant/dequant cost gets amplified. can we add a perf counter for `kv_hit_rate` per route?

te-bot: transformer-engine CI: deployment 2.3.2 -> canary group A (10%) scheduled 2026-03-18T14:00Z. Watch for regressions on L40S.

ryan: FYI profiling details: on H100 we saw fused_fp8_attn has better throughput for seq>=256 and stable kv hits. For seq<=128 cutlass_attn wins. On L40S the memory bandwidth characteristics change the crossover point — move threshold to 192 for L40S.

dmitri: Action items I can take: 1) Add 90th-percentile kernel-selection heuristic (PR coming) 2) Instrument kv_hit_rate and per-route fp8_hotpath metric 3) Add an opt-in per-model `fp8_mode: auto|force|fallback` flag for canaries.

ashley: Also add a short test in perf-regression suite: low-kv-hit synthetic workload (random prompt IDs) and mixed seq_len traffic. We'll gate TE upgrades on that.

natalie: For the correctness anomalies — logs show rare NaN/backprop divergence in fp8 path for some older checkpoints. root cause might be quant calibration tables created at rollout time. repro steps: run `python tools/calibrate_fp8.py --model xyz --calib-seeds 4` and compare outputs. temporary fix: reuse calibration artifacts from pre-2.3.2 until we fix stable calibration in TE.

ryan: TL;DR: immediate mitigations: pin TE to 2.3.1 for production L40S pools, enable kernel-selection percentile heuristic, add kv_hit_rate metric, and add fp8_fallback_seq_threshold=192 for L40S. Longer term: refine calibration flow and upstream a perf-stable fused kernel.

natalie: I'll open the canary rollback PR and create the perf task list. assigning dmitri + ashley to follow-ups. thanks :thumbsup:
